solutions.title: AI meeting devices for teams
solutions.short: Compare recorders, subscription ownership and team workflows before a bulk purchase.
solutions.question: Which device fits our team?
overview: This page is for managers and distributors preparing to buy AI recording devices, such as the TicNote range, for a team. Trying one recorder yourself is easy. A team purchase raises a different set of questions: who owns the subscription, who reviews the notes, where exports go and what happens to an account when someone leaves. We suggest answering them with a small, measurable pilot before choosing a model and quantity.

CNPS provides the selection and pilot method, checks destination availability and issues a formal quotation. Transcription performance, enterprise features and bulk terms depend on the exact model and the written quote. We do not substitute vendor demonstrations or other people’s experience for your own test results.

scenarios.title: Project meetings across languages
scenarios.text: Teams that switch between Chinese, English or Arabic need to confirm how the device transcribes real accents and technical terms, and whether the correction time is acceptable.

scenarios.title: Field visits and customer calls
scenarios.text: Sales or engineering staff record conversations in noisy places. Test distance, noise and battery behavior, and agree how people are informed and give consent to recording.

scenarios.title: Distributors configuring bulk orders
scenarios.text: Channel partners need to confirm destination compatibility, subscription activation, warranty handling and replacement procedures before shipping, and write them into the supply terms.

solutions.deliverable: A clearer device and subscription shortlist
solutions.input: Destination country, team size, meeting languages, recording environment and target date.
checks: Compare the exact SKU and included subscription.
Test transcription and the time needed to correct notes.
Check export formats, account ownership and reassignment.
Confirm regional availability, warranty and bulk terms.

steps.title: Choose the pilot group and meeting sample
steps.text: Pick three to five people who represent typical users, covering real languages, room sizes and remote calls. Record how long notes take today before the pilot starts, so you have a baseline.

steps.title: Compare candidate models on the same meetings
steps.text: Test the candidate devices and their included subscriptions on the same sample. Record missed statements, name errors, action-item errors and the minutes needed to reach a usable note.

steps.title: Check data flow and account ownership
steps.text: Go through export formats, storage location, sharing and deletion. Confirm whether subscriptions can be reassigned, whether team administration exists and who controls recordings after a departure.

steps.title: Build the shortlist and request a quotation
steps.text: Summarize models, quantity, destination, languages and timing into a quotation request. CNPS verifies availability and bulk terms and quotes in writing for the exact model.

mistakes.title: Treating transcription speed as time saved
mistakes.text: A fast transcript is not a usable note. Only when correction, distribution and action-item follow-up are counted can you tell whether the team actually saved time.

mistakes.title: Inferring team administration from consumer features
mistakes.text: Account transfer, central management and enterprise features vary by model and plan. Confirm them in writing for the selected model before ordering instead of assuming them.

mistakes.title: Ignoring recording notice and consent
mistakes.text: Countries and meeting settings have different recording requirements. Agree the notice, the consent record and the handling of sensitive content before the pilot starts.

glossary.title: Exact SKU
glossary.text: The precise model and variant on the quotation, including region, color and bundled plan. Two devices with the same product name can ship with different subscriptions and warranty terms.

glossary.title: Included subscription
glossary.text: The transcription or note plan bundled with the device, its duration and what happens when it expires. Renewal price and who pays it belong in the pilot record.

glossary.title: Subscription ownership
glossary.text: Whether the plan is tied to an individual account or to the organization, and whether it can be reassigned when a team member leaves.

glossary.title: Team administration
glossary.text: Central features such as adding and removing users, managing shared notes and exporting on behalf of others. Availability varies by model and plan.

glossary.title: Correction time
glossary.text: The minutes an editor needs to turn the raw transcript into a note the team can act on. It is a better measure than transcription speed.

glossary.title: Export format
glossary.text: The file types and destinations notes can be sent to, such as text, DOCX, PDF or a cloud folder, and whether audio can be exported as well.

glossary.title: Recording notice and consent
glossary.text: How participants are informed that a meeting is recorded and how their agreement is documented, according to local rules and company policy.

glossary.title: Warranty and replacement (RMA)
glossary.text: Who handles a faulty unit in the destination country, how long replacement takes and whether a spare pool is needed for a team rollout.

metrics.title: Baseline minutes per meeting
metrics.text: Before the pilot, record how long a typical note takes today from the end of the meeting to distribution. Every later comparison is measured against this number.

metrics.title: Correction minutes per transcript
metrics.text: For each recorded meeting, count the minutes from opening the raw transcript to a note the team accepts. Compare the median across devices, not the best case.

metrics.title: Missed statements and wrong names
metrics.text: Count omitted decisions, misattributed speakers and misspelled names or product terms per meeting. Note which languages and rooms produce the most errors.

metrics.title: Action-item accuracy
metrics.text: Check whether the generated action items match what the group agreed, including owner and date. A note with wrong owners creates work instead of saving it.

metrics.title: Battery, range and failure events
metrics.text: Log battery level after each meeting, distance and noise conditions, and every failed recording, sync or export, so hardware reliability is judged on evidence.

solutions.boundaries: Team administration and enterprise features vary by product. Confirm them for the selected model before ordering.

faq.question: Can CNPS guarantee a device’s transcription accuracy?
faq.answer: No. Accuracy depends on language, accent, noise and terminology, and published figures do not replace your own meeting sample. We suggest testing on real meetings using the steps above.

faq.question: Do we need a pilot before a bulk purchase?
faq.answer: We recommend a representative pilot with a few devices. It exposes subscription ownership, export and noise issues before you commit to a quantity, at far lower cost than bulk returns.

faq.question: What information is needed for a quotation?
faq.answer: Destination country, expected quantity, main use, meeting languages, expected timing and whether you want samples first. Specific details make availability checks and term confirmation faster.

faq.question: How long should a device pilot run?
faq.answer: Two to four weeks of normal meetings is usually enough to see accents, room types and remote calls, and to settle into a real note workflow. Shorter pilots tend to reflect novelty rather than everyday use.

faq.question: Can the same device serve Chinese, English and Arabic meetings?
faq.answer: Language support differs by model and plan, and performance differs again by accent and terminology. Test each language you actually use on the same device rather than relying on a supported-language list.

faq.question: Who should own the subscriptions after the pilot?
faq.answer: Decide before ordering. If notes belong to the organization, the plan should be administered centrally and be reassignable. Personal accounts are simpler to start but harder to recover when someone leaves.

solutions.title: Knowledge assistants grounded in your documents
solutions.short: Define a private knowledge or support workflow around real questions, permissions and evidence.
solutions.question: Can AI answer from our documents?
overview: This page is for IT leaders, service providers and business owners who want AI to answer questions from their own documents. Product manuals, internal policies and support knowledge bases can all become source material. What determines the value is not the model name, but whether the question set is real, permissions are clear and citations can be checked.

CNPS helps define the evaluation scope, prepare the evaluation set and agree acceptance, and can discuss implementation with open-source options such as FastGPT where appropriate. Public projects such as Dify, RAGFlow, Qwen and DeepSeek are research starting points, not CNPS customer deliveries. Implementation scope and software licensing are agreed separately.

scenarios.title: Product manual and technical support Q&A
scenarios.text: After-sales or support teams need accurate answers from manuals in several versions, with the source visible. Evaluate how version conflicts are handled and whether citations truly support the answer.

scenarios.title: Internal policy and process lookup
scenarios.text: Staff ask about expenses, approvals or compliance steps. Evaluate permission boundaries: each role should only retrieve the documents it is allowed to see, and outdated policies must be retired promptly.

scenarios.title: First-pass triage of multilingual inquiries
scenarios.text: Export teams receive inquiries in Chinese, English or Arabic and need a first answer from product materials before human review. Evaluate target-language performance and refusal behavior.

solutions.input: Authorized sample documents, target languages, expected users, hosting requirements and a business owner.
checks: Build an evaluation set with expected answers.
Verify citations, model version and refusal behavior.
Test document permissions and update procedures.
Compare full running cost and human review time.

steps.title: Fix one task and a business owner
steps.text: Choose one workflow, one set of authorized documents and one person accountable for answer quality. Identify outdated and conflicting versions and decide first which document is authoritative.

steps.title: Build the evaluation set before tuning
steps.text: Follow the resource method: everyday factual questions, cross-document comparisons, questions that should be refused for lack of evidence, and permission tests. Agree the set and thresholds before seeing results.

steps.title: Compare candidates on the same set
steps.text: Fix documents, prompts and model versions. Business reviewers compare correctness, citation support, refusals and latency, and record the time needed to correct each answer by hand.

steps.title: Settle operations and cost before expanding
steps.text: Document who updates content, approves access, reviews wrong answers and handles model changes, and map every external model call. Count hosting, inference, ingestion, support and human review before scaling.

mistakes.title: Replacing your own data test with public leaderboards
mistakes.text: Rankings reflect general tasks, not your documents, terminology and language. Performance on the same evaluation set is the basis for selection.

mistakes.title: Swapping hard questions after seeing results
mistakes.text: Removing failures from the set distorts the evaluation. Keep failed results and separate tuning questions from held-out tests, so you know how the assistant will behave in production.

mistakes.title: Equating open-source availability with free commercial use
mistakes.text: Open-source licenses carry additional conditions, such as multi-tenant and branding restrictions. Check the license of the exact version and the hosting terms before launch.

glossary.title: Evaluation set
glossary.text: A fixed list of real questions with expected answers, sources and pass criteria, agreed before any tuning. It is the yardstick for every candidate.

glossary.title: Retrieval-augmented generation (RAG)
glossary.text: The approach where the assistant retrieves passages from your documents and answers from them, rather than from general training data alone.

glossary.title: Citation
glossary.text: The reference the assistant shows for an answer. A citation counts only if the cited passage actually supports the statement when a reviewer opens it.

glossary.title: Refusal behavior
glossary.text: What the assistant does when the documents contain no answer. A correct refusal is a pass; an invented answer is a fail even if it sounds plausible.

glossary.title: Permission boundary
glossary.text: The rule that each user role can only retrieve the documents it is allowed to see, tested with role-specific questions.

glossary.title: Business owner
glossary.text: The named person accountable for answer quality, document updates and the decision to expand or stop.

glossary.title: Held-out test
glossary.text: Questions kept aside from tuning and run only at the end, so the result shows how the assistant behaves on questions it has not been adjusted for.

glossary.title: Total running cost
glossary.text: Hosting, inference, ingestion, licensing, support and human review time added together per month, not the model API price alone.

metrics.title: Correct answers on the evaluation set
metrics.text: The share of questions answered correctly according to the business reviewer, reported separately for everyday, cross-document and target-language questions.

metrics.title: Citation support rate
metrics.text: The share of citations that, when opened, actually support the answer. An answer with a decorative citation is counted as unsupported.

metrics.title: Correct refusals
metrics.text: How often the assistant declines questions that have no answer in the documents, and how often it invents one instead.

metrics.title: Permission test results
metrics.text: The number of role-specific questions where a user could retrieve a document outside their permission. The acceptable number is zero.

metrics.title: Review minutes and cost per answer
metrics.text: The average time a reviewer spends checking or correcting an answer, together with hosting, inference and ingestion cost per month.

solutions.boundaries: Implementation scope and software licensing need to be agreed. Open-source availability does not establish unrestricted resale rights.

faq.question: How many documents do we need to start?
faq.answer: Start with the authorized documents one workflow needs; a few dozen is often enough for a meaningful evaluation set. A small, authoritative scope is worth more than a large, uncleaned archive.

faq.question: Will the evaluation send our documents to third parties?
faq.answer: It depends on the deployment and the model services chosen. Even a self-hosted application may send data to external model or speech services. We suggest evaluating with non-sensitive documents first and mapping every data flow.

faq.question: Does CNPS handle implementation?
faq.answer: CNPS first helps define scope, the evaluation set and acceptance. Implementation capacity, commercial scope and software licensing are agreed separately for each requirement and are not included by default in the evaluation.

faq.question: Can the assistant run entirely on our own servers?
faq.answer: Self-hosted deployment is possible with several open-source applications, but the language, embedding and speech models it calls may still be external services. Map every call before deciding what “on-premises” means for your data.

faq.question: How do we keep answers current when documents change?
faq.answer: Name the person who updates content, define how retired documents are removed from retrieval and re-run part of the evaluation set after each significant update. An assistant without an update routine drifts out of date quietly.

faq.question: Which languages can be evaluated?
faq.answer: Chinese, English and Arabic questions can all be included, but performance differs by question language and by document language. Build target-language questions into the evaluation set rather than assuming results transfer.

solutions.title: Edge AI for a defined camera task
solutions.short: Plan the whole site: cameras, compute, network, installation and a measurable acceptance test.
solutions.question: Will edge AI work at our site?
overview: This page is for integrators and site owners who need a camera recognition task deployed at a factory, farm, campus or commercial site. Edge AI keeps recognition on site, but whether it works depends on the whole system: cameras, compute, network, installation, storage and operations, not just the compute rating of one board.

CNPS helps organize site requirements, run a representative site test and produce an evaluation brief. Deployment references published by vendors such as Seeed show what is possible, but they are not CNPS deliveries and do not guarantee the same result under your lighting, distances and network conditions.

scenarios.title: Safety and compliance monitoring on production lines or in warehouses
scenarios.text: Detect missing protective equipment, boundary crossing or unusual dwelling. Evaluate whether the false-alarm rate lets staff trust alerts over time, and how the system performs at night and in backlight.

scenarios.title: Continuous observation in farming and agriculture
scenarios.text: Count animals or crops, or recognize behavior and condition. Evaluate the long-term effect of dust, humidity and changing light on the cameras and compute units.

scenarios.title: Local recognition at network-constrained sites
scenarios.text: Remote sites, or sites that cannot send video to the cloud, need local recognition with only results uploaded. Evaluate behavior during disconnection, recovery and local storage capacity.

solutions.deliverable: A site requirement and evaluation brief
solutions.input: Camera types, site layout, lighting, objects to detect, network conditions and the operational owner.
checks: Agree on the detection task and ground truth.
Record false alarms, misses and end-to-end latency.
Test lighting changes, disconnection and recovery.
Include installation, storage and support in the cost.

steps.title: Agree the detection task and ground truth
steps.text: State in one sentence what to detect, under which conditions and who acts on an alert. Agree how ground truth is produced and which false-alarm and miss levels are acceptable at acceptance.

steps.title: Complete the site survey and collect representative footage
steps.text: Use the edge AI site survey to record camera types, mounting positions, lighting, distances, network and power. Collect footage at different times of day, including the worst conditions.

steps.title: Test candidate configurations on real footage
steps.text: Compare camera and compute combinations on the same footage. Record false alarms, misses and end-to-end latency, and simulate lighting changes, disconnection and device restarts.

steps.title: Cost the full system and write the evaluation brief
steps.text: Include installation, cabling, storage, spares, support and operating staff in the cost per camera and per site. The brief becomes the shared basis for the quotation and acceptance.

mistakes.title: Judging site performance from demonstration videos
mistakes.text: Demonstrations are usually filmed under ideal lighting and distance. Your site has to be tested under its worst conditions to know whether the system will keep running.

mistakes.title: Comparing only model inference time
mistakes.text: End-to-end latency includes capture, transmission, inference and alert delivery. Only the full chain tells you whether an alert arrives in time for someone to act.

mistakes.title: Leaving out installation and operating costs
mistakes.text: The board price is a small part. Cabling, enclosures, storage, spares and remote maintenance often decide whether a project is sustainable.

glossary.title: Detection task
glossary.text: One sentence stating what to detect, under which conditions and who acts on the result. Everything else on the site is measured against it.

glossary.title: Ground truth
glossary.text: The human-verified record of what actually happened in the footage, used to judge whether each alert was right or wrong.

glossary.title: False alarm and miss
glossary.text: A false alarm is an alert with no real event; a miss is a real event with no alert. Both rates are needed, because tuning one usually moves the other.

glossary.title: End-to-end latency
glossary.text: The time from the event in front of the camera to the alert reaching the person who acts, including capture, transmission, inference and delivery.

glossary.title: Edge device / compute unit
glossary.text: The on-site computer that runs recognition, such as a Jetson-class or NPU board. Its rating matters less than its behavior under heat, dust and power interruptions.

glossary.title: Site survey
glossary.text: The structured record of camera types, mounting positions, lighting, distances, network and power at each location, completed before any equipment is chosen.

glossary.title: Acceptance criteria
glossary.text: The false-alarm, miss and latency levels agreed in advance that decide whether the installation is accepted and paid for.

glossary.title: Cost per camera, per site
glossary.text: The full figure including cameras, compute, cabling, enclosures, storage, spares, installation labor, support and operating staff.

metrics.title: False-alarm rate per camera per day
metrics.text: Count alerts with no real event, by camera and by time of day. A rate staff can live with for weeks is the real threshold, not the vendor’s demonstration figure.

metrics.title: Miss rate against ground truth
metrics.text: Compare alerts with the verified record of real events. Report misses separately for daytime, night, backlight and the worst weather you collected.

metrics.title: End-to-end latency
metrics.text: Measure from the event in the footage to the alert on the responder’s screen or phone. Record the median and the slowest ten percent.

metrics.title: Uptime, disconnection and recovery
metrics.text: Log every device restart, network loss and how long recognition and uploads took to recover, including whether local storage kept the results.

metrics.title: Cost per camera and per site
metrics.text: Add cameras, compute, cabling, enclosures, storage, spares, installation and support, then divide by the number of cameras and sites you actually plan to run.

solutions.boundaries: Hardware capability and demonstration videos do not guarantee performance in your environment. A representative site test is needed.

faq.question: Do we have to buy equipment before evaluating?
faq.answer: Usually not. Complete the site survey and footage collection first, then test with a small number of representative devices. Buying in volume before the task and acceptance criteria are clear carries more risk.

faq.question: Can CNPS supply a ready-made recognition solution?
faq.answer: CNPS provides requirement organization, the site evaluation method and hardware sourcing. Whether a recognition task is feasible depends on your site conditions and must be shown by a representative test, not by applying a template.

faq.question: What accuracy can we expect?
faq.answer: We do not promise accuracy before testing. False alarms, misses and latency should be measured on your real footage and judged against acceptance criteria agreed in advance.

faq.question: Can we reuse the cameras we already have?
faq.answer: Often partly. Resolution, lens angle, night performance and stream format all affect recognition. Include existing cameras in the site test and be prepared to replace those that fail the worst-condition footage.

faq.question: How long does a representative site test take?
faq.answer: Collecting footage across times of day and weather usually takes one to three weeks, and the comparison itself a further week or two. Rushing the footage stage is the most common reason results do not hold after installation.

faq.question: What happens to the video and the results?
faq.answer: Decide before testing where footage is stored, for how long, who can view it and what leaves the site. Local recognition can limit data transfer, but retention and access rules still need an owner.

solutions.title: Voice interfaces, from idea to prototype
solutions.short: Scope an ESP32-based voice device together with the backend services it needs to keep working.
solutions.question: How do we prototype a voice device?
overview: This page is for product teams, OEMs and exhibition owners who want to prototype a voice interaction device on low-cost hardware such as the ESP32. Open firmware puts a first prototype within reach, but the device is only the start of a service: speech recognition, models, content and credential management decide whether it keeps working.

CNPS helps define the prototype scope, map dependencies and plan tests. Open-source projects such as XiaoZhi ESP32 are technical references, not a CNPS product supply or service contract. A working prototype is not a mass-production commitment; product testing, supply and commercial rights are assessed separately.

scenarios.title: Reception or exhibition Q&A terminal
scenarios.text: Visitors ask about exhibits, directions or opening hours by voice. Evaluate wake-up and recognition in noise, interruption handling and who is responsible for content updates.

scenarios.title: Voice companion prototype for an existing product
scenarios.text: Add a voice entry point to a current product and check whether users accept it. Evaluate the acoustic fit of microphone and enclosure, latency and the service cost of each conversation.

scenarios.title: Multilingual reception
scenarios.text: Serve Chinese, English or Arabic speakers. Evaluate recognition in each language, speech synthesis quality and language switching, and whether the content is authorized.

solutions.deliverable: A prototype scope and dependency checklist
solutions.input: One intended task, users, languages, acoustic conditions, expected volume and maintenance owner.
checks: Specify microphones, speakers, power and network.
Map speech, model and content service dependencies.
Test interruption, noise and network loss.
Plan firmware recovery, credentials and service cost.

steps.title: Fix one task and authorized content
steps.text: Do one thing only, such as answering questions about a single product line. Prepare authorized content and expected questions, and state the intended users and volume.

steps.title: Specify hardware and the dependency list
steps.text: Use the voice prototype specification to list microphone, speaker, power and network needs, and map the provider, region and billing of every speech, model and content service.

steps.title: Test in the real acoustic environment
steps.text: Test noise, distance, interruption and network loss where the device will actually be used. Record recognition errors, response latency and recovery instead of demonstrating in a quiet office.

steps.title: Plan the lifecycle before discussing the next step
steps.text: Agree firmware recovery, credential rotation, service shutdown and content updates, and estimate the monthly service cost per device. Then discuss product testing, supply and commercial rights.

mistakes.title: Counting only hardware cost
mistakes.text: ESP32 boards are inexpensive, but recognition, model and synthesis services bill by usage. Record the cost per conversation during the prototype so it does not escape control after rollout.

mistakes.title: Rolling out after a quiet-room demonstration
mistakes.text: Exhibition halls, receptions and street fronts differ enormously in noise and echo. A prototype untested in its target environment is not a basis for deployment.

mistakes.title: Ignoring license and trademark boundaries
mistakes.text: The firmware’s open-source license does not cover the cloud services, voices, product design or trademarks used. Check each item before a public release.

glossary.title: Wake word
glossary.text: The phrase that switches the device from listening for its name to processing a request. False wakes in noise and missed wakes at distance are both measured.

glossary.title: Speech recognition (ASR)
glossary.text: The service that turns speech into text. It is usually a cloud service billed per minute or per request, with its own language coverage and region.

glossary.title: Speech synthesis (TTS)
glossary.text: The service that produces the spoken reply. Voice quality, language support and licensing for public use are separate questions.

glossary.title: Barge-in / interruption handling
glossary.text: What happens when a user speaks while the device is still replying. Poor handling makes a demo feel slow in real use.

glossary.title: Dependency map
glossary.text: The list of every external service the device calls, with provider, region, credential owner and billing, so nobody is surprised when one changes.

glossary.title: Cost per conversation
glossary.text: Recognition, model and synthesis charges added together for one typical exchange, then multiplied by expected volume per device per month.

glossary.title: Firmware recovery
glossary.text: How a device is updated or restored in the field when firmware, credentials or a service endpoint changes, without sending it back.

glossary.title: Authorized content
glossary.text: The questions the device is allowed to answer and the material it may answer from, agreed with the content owner before the prototype goes in front of people.

metrics.title: Wake and recognition errors by environment
metrics.text: Count false wakes, missed wakes and misrecognized requests at the real location, separately for quiet periods, peak noise and each language.

metrics.title: Response latency
metrics.text: Time from the end of the user’s sentence to the start of the spoken reply. Record the median and the slowest cases, and note which service caused the delay.

metrics.title: Interruption and recovery behavior
metrics.text: Log what happens when a user interrupts, when the network drops mid-reply and when the device restarts, and how long it takes to become usable again.

metrics.title: Cost per conversation and per device per month
metrics.text: Sum recognition, model and synthesis charges for typical exchanges during the prototype and project them to the expected volume.

metrics.title: Content coverage and refusals
metrics.text: Track how many real visitor questions fell inside the authorized content, how many were refused correctly and how many were answered outside scope.

solutions.boundaries: A working prototype is not a mass-production commitment. Product testing, supply and commercial rights must be assessed separately.

faq.question: Will CNPS manufacture the voice device for us?
faq.answer: In the prototype phase CNPS helps define scope, dependencies and tests. Mass production involves product testing, supply, certification and commercial rights, which are assessed and agreed separately after the prototype is validated.

faq.question: Is the prototype suitable for children or the public?
faq.answer: A working demonstration does not establish content safety, child suitability or regulatory conformity. Assess content boundaries, privacy and safety specifically before a public deployment.

faq.question: Does the device work when the network is down?
faq.answer: It depends on the architecture. Most voice functions rely on backend services, so the device needs clear prompts and recovery behavior during disconnection. This case must be covered in testing.

faq.question: Which hardware do we need for a first prototype?
faq.answer: An ESP32-class development board with a microphone array, a speaker and stable power is usually enough to test the interaction. Enclosure acoustics and industrial-grade parts become relevant only after the task and environment are confirmed.

faq.question: Can the device use our own model or knowledge base?
faq.answer: Usually yes, because the firmware calls backend services you configure. The question to evaluate is whether that backend answers correctly within acceptable latency and cost, which is tested the same way as a knowledge assistant.

faq.question: What should we prepare before the field test?
faq.answer: The authorized content, a list of expected questions, the target location at its busiest time, a way to log every exchange and the person who will judge which answers were acceptable.

solutions.title: Robotics for research and controlled pilots
solutions.short: Clarify the exact hardware, SDK access, accessories and local support before procurement.
solutions.question: What does our robotics lab need?
overview: This page is for people planning to buy quadruped robots, robotic arms or similar platforms for university labs, research institutes or corporate innovation teams. Public SDKs and demonstration videos make robotics research look more accessible, but procurement has to state the exact edition, developer access, accessories, training and who provides local support.

CNPS helps prepare the configuration and support checklist and verifies supply and destination terms. Public materials such as Unitree SDK2 and the UFACTORY xArm SDK are evaluation starting points; they do not mean every product edition has the same access, and they are not CNPS customer orders. Site safety and integration need qualified owners.

scenarios.title: Locomotion control and perception research
scenarios.text: Labs need to validate algorithms on a real platform. Evaluate whether the chosen edition opens low-level control interfaces and whether the operating system and SDK versions are compatible.

scenarios.title: Controlled grasping and assembly pilots
scenarios.text: Use an arm to pick, place or assemble a limited set of workpieces. Evaluate the workpiece, gripper, payload, reach and camera arrangement, and record repeatable success rates.

scenarios.title: Teaching and talent development
scenarios.text: Several students share one platform in turns. Evaluate training, spare parts, emergency procedures and supervised operating rules, not only the robot body.

solutions.input: Research task, exact platform, payload, workspace, developer access, destination and trained operator.
checks: Confirm the SKU and developer permissions in writing.
Check operating system and SDK compatibility.
Include tools, fixtures, spare parts and training.
Define supervised testing and emergency procedures.

steps.title: Write down the research task and the exact platform
steps.text: Derive requirements from the task: payload, workspace, sensors, developer access and destination. Robots with the same name can have different access by edition, so name the exact model.

steps.title: Confirm SDK access and compatibility in writing
steps.text: Ask the supplier for written confirmation of developer access, supported operating systems and SDK versions for the selected edition, and check them against the lab’s existing software environment.

steps.title: Start with simulation and supervised tests
steps.text: Validate the workflow in simulation first, then run supervised tests inside a bounded workspace. Record successful attempts and every failure, and agree emergency stops and procedures.

steps.title: Put the full configuration into the procurement request
steps.text: Use the robotics procurement resource to list tools, fixtures, spares, training, shipping and local support, name the owners for safety and maintenance, then request a quotation.

mistakes.title: Assuming a public SDK applies to every edition
mistakes.text: Education, standard and developer editions may open different interfaces. Obtain written confirmation for the exact edition before purchasing.

mistakes.title: Buying only the robot body
mistakes.text: Grippers, fixtures, cameras, spares, training and shipping often decide whether the project can start. Missing any one of them can leave equipment idle for months.

mistakes.title: Inferring autonomy from demonstration videos
mistakes.text: International demonstration videos show possibilities, not proof of autonomous productivity. Whether your research task succeeds depends on your algorithms, scenario and operating skills.

glossary.title: Exact edition
glossary.text: The precise product variant, such as education, standard or developer, named on the quotation. Editions with the same body can expose different interfaces.

glossary.title: Developer access / low-level control
glossary.text: Whether the edition lets your code command joints, motors or gait directly, rather than only through a high-level app or teach pendant.

glossary.title: SDK version compatibility
glossary.text: The operating system, ROS distribution, Python and library versions the platform supports, checked against what the lab already runs.

glossary.title: Payload and reach
glossary.text: The mass the arm or robot can carry and the workspace it can cover, stated for the exact configuration including gripper and camera.

glossary.title: End effector / gripper
glossary.text: The tool mounted on the arm for the task. It is usually ordered separately and decides whether the workpieces in your study can be handled at all.

glossary.title: Bounded workspace
glossary.text: The physical area where the robot may operate during tests, with guarding, emergency stops and clear rules for who may be inside it.

glossary.title: Repeatable success rate
glossary.text: The share of attempts that complete the task across many runs under the same conditions, recorded with every failure rather than the best demonstration.

glossary.title: Local support and spares
glossary.text: Who repairs the platform in your country, how long parts take to arrive and which consumables should be stocked before the first test.

metrics.title: Written confirmations received
metrics.text: Track which items the supplier has confirmed in writing for the exact edition: developer access, supported operating systems, SDK versions, warranty and destination terms.

metrics.title: Compatibility results
metrics.text: Record whether the SDK installs and runs on the lab’s existing machines, which versions were needed and how long setup took before the first command was sent.

metrics.title: Task success rate and failure log
metrics.text: Count successful and failed attempts under the same conditions, with the cause of each failure, so autonomy is judged on repeated runs rather than a demonstration.

metrics.title: Safety incidents and near-misses
metrics.text: Log every emergency stop, boundary breach and unplanned movement during supervised tests, and what changed in the procedure afterwards.

metrics.title: Time and cost to first experiment
metrics.text: Measure the calendar time and full cost from order to the first completed experiment, including accessories, training, shipping, customs and any idle weeks waiting for parts.

solutions.boundaries: References to SDKs do not mean every product edition has the same access. Site safety and integration require qualified owners.

faq.question: Which robotics platforms can CNPS provide?
faq.answer: CNPS verifies the exact editions, accessories and destination terms that can be supplied for your requirement and prepares the configuration list. Supply and access for any platform are subject to written confirmation from the supplier.

faq.question: What site conditions should we prepare in advance?
faq.answer: A bounded workspace, emergency stops and guarding, qualified operators and a maintenance owner. Put these in place before the equipment arrives rather than afterwards.

faq.question: Can we rent or trial a platform first?
faq.answer: Trial and rental options depend on the platform and region. State the research task and timeline in your inquiry so feasible evaluation options can be verified together.

faq.question: Should we start with a robotic arm or a quadruped?
faq.answer: It follows from the research task. Grasping, assembly and workpiece studies point to an arm; locomotion, perception and outdoor navigation point to a legged platform. Write the task down first and let the platform follow.

faq.question: What does a typical robotics quotation include?
faq.answer: The exact edition, developer access, accessories such as grippers and cameras, spares, training, shipping and destination terms, each as a separate line. Anything missing from the quotation should be assumed not included.

faq.question: How do we plan for maintenance after delivery?
faq.answer: Name a maintenance owner, stock the consumables the supplier recommends, confirm who repairs the platform in your country and how long parts take, and keep a log of every fault from the first week.

solutionsIndex.chooseText: Each solution begins with a buyer question. The rows below show what you receive, what to prepare and the first thing to check, so you can pick the page closest to your situation.
solutionsIndex.prepText: Five things that make the first conversation useful, whichever solution you choose.

prep.title: Name one task
prep.text: Describe the single workflow or site you want to improve, not the whole organization. A narrow task makes the pilot measurable and the quotation exact.

prep.title: Know your destination and timing
prep.text: Country, expected quantity and the date you need results by decide availability, shipping and whether a sample stage is realistic.

prep.title: Record today’s baseline
prep.text: How long the work takes now, how often it fails and what it costs. Without a baseline, no pilot can show an improvement.

prep.title: Identify the decision owner
prep.text: The person who will judge the pilot and sign the order. Their acceptance criteria should be written down before the test begins.

prep.title: Separate must-haves from preferences
prep.text: Data location, language support, warranty and administration features that are non-negotiable belong in the inquiry; everything else can be discussed.

solutionsIndex.termsText: The same words appear on every solution page, in the resources and in our quotations. Here is what we mean by them.

terms.title: Pilot
terms.text: A small, time-boxed test with real users, real data and agreed metrics, run before any volume commitment.

terms.title: Baseline
terms.text: The measured state of the work before the pilot, used as the reference for every later comparison.

terms.title: Acceptance criteria
terms.text: The measurable results agreed in advance that decide whether a pilot or delivery is accepted.

terms.title: Exact SKU or edition
terms.text: The precise product variant named on the quotation. Products with the same name can differ in features, access and warranty.

terms.title: Destination availability
terms.text: Whether a product can be supplied, activated, warranted and supported in the buyer’s country, confirmed before quoting.

terms.title: Request for quotation (RFQ)
terms.text: The written summary of task, quantity, destination, languages and timing from which CNPS prepares a formal quotation.

terms.title: Industry reference
terms.text: A public case or open-source project cited to show what is possible. It is not a CNPS customer delivery and does not promise the same result.

terms.title: Full cost
terms.text: Hardware, subscriptions, hosting, installation, training, support and review time added together over the period you plan to run the solution.

cases.title: Dify 在日本：从实验走向企业工作流程
cases.label: 厂商发布的客户案例
cases.summary: 公开客户故事将流程构建与全公司采用和治理联系起来。
cases.facts: Dify 发布的 Kakaku.com 案例介绍了采用 Dify Enterprise 组织 AI 应用开发的过程。其 GitHub 仓库提供工作流、检索和自托管文档。这是厂商叙述，不是独立审计。
cases.lesson: 采购时应关注流程如何被团队实际使用：谁负责、谁能访问数据、错误如何升级处理。CNPS 建议从一个文档或支持流程及约定的评估题集开始。
cases.limits: 这不是 CNPS 交付项目。已报告的采用情况不能证明新客户项目的结果。Dify 许可对多租户使用及前端品牌标识有附加条件。
evaluation: 使用授权文档和固定题集。
衡量引用正确性及人工修正时间。
测试权限与证据不足时的拒答。

cases.title: Qwen 与 DeepSeek：降低首次评估门槛
cases.label: 开源与传播渠道参考
cases.summary: 英文技术资料与公开评估渠道降低了试用模型所需的投入。
cases.facts: Qwen3 和 DeepSeek-R1 均维护公开仓库，提供模型和使用信息。Qwen 官方 X 帖子将模型发布与本地使用及在线体验相连接。一条与 Arena 相关的公开 X 帖子记录了 DeepSeek-R1 进入国际评估渠道。
cases.lesson: 买家需要可复现的任务、明确的模型版本及成本边界。使用相同文档和问题评估候选模型，并包含应当拒答的问题。
cases.limits: 这些参考不能证明收入、当前模型优势或在您数据上的表现。请核对确切模型检查点、许可、基础设施及服务条款。
evaluation: 固定数据集、提示词和模型版本。
比较正确性、引用、延迟和每项完成任务的成本。
测试目标语言与真实并发使用。
sources: Qwen 的 X 帖子 · 2025年8月13日

cases.title: RAGFlow：优先评估文档处理层
cases.label: 开源技术参考
cases.summary: 为需要从复杂文档生成可追溯答案的检索流程提供实用参考。
cases.facts: RAGFlow 仓库介绍了文档处理、检索、来源引用和自托管方法。它是评估文档流程的技术来源，不是 CNPS 客户部署的证据。
cases.lesson: 产品手册包含版本差异、单位与例外。在选择模型前，应确定权威文档以及如何移除过时信息。
cases.limits: 仓库列出的文档支持范围不保证特定扫描件或表格的提取质量。应按选定版本验证算力需求与依赖版本。
evaluation: 纳入表格、扫描件和相互冲突的文档版本。
检查引用段落能否支持具体答案。
测试更新、删除及访问边界。

cases.title: Seeed 与 Intflow：基于边缘硬件的本地行业方案
cases.label: 厂商发布的部署参考
cases.summary: 畜牧监测参考展示了应用专业能力与边缘设备的合作方式。
cases.facts: PNY 托管的 Seeed 案例集介绍了 Intflow 的畜牧监测方案，列出韩国、西班牙、日本、奥地利和波兰的部署，并指出方案使用了 Seeed reComputer 设备。
cases.lesson: 可借鉴的模式是：本地行业专家负责应用和现场客户关系，硬件供应商支持设备平台。应规划完整系统，包括摄像头与持续服务。
cases.limits: 材料由厂商发布，此处不将其宣称的改善效果用作预测。它不能证明 CNPS 拥有分销关系，也不能证明适用于新现场。
evaluation: 明确动物或识别对象及观察条件。
使用具有代表性的影像及约定的真实标注。
计算每台摄像头和每个现场的总成本。
sources: PNY 托管的 Seeed 案例集

cases.title: Seeed：从硬件演示连接到工程文档
cases.label: 官方工程资料与 X 参考
cases.summary: 展示配置与工程实施路径后，演示才更有助于采购决策。
cases.facts: Seeed 官方 X 帖子介绍了四摄像头边缘配置。其公开 Wiki 仓库及定制服务分别提供工程与生命周期资料，覆盖需求、验证和生产。
cases.lesson: 短视频可以介绍可能性。采购页面随后应提供系统图、设备清单、环境假设及供工程师评估的测试计划。
cases.limits: X 帖子属于演示声明，不能证明独立性能测量或现成的 CNPS 方案。应按选定配置检查兼容性。
evaluation: 列出摄像头接口、计算模块与软件版本。
测量端到端延迟，不只测模型推理。
测试故障恢复与持续运行。
sources: Seeed 的 X 帖子 · 2025年12月26日

cases.title: 小智 ESP32：设备只是服务的起点
cases.label: 开源技术参考
cases.summary: 开放固件让语音原型更易实现，而后端和生命周期选择决定其实用性。
cases.facts: 小智 ESP32 仓库提供语音交互固件及多语言文档，README 介绍模型与 MCP 连接。它是固件参考，不是完整的产品供货或服务合同。
cases.lesson: 接待或展览原型应从一项任务与授权内容开始。除外壳外，还应明确麦克风、网络及后端，并测试真实声学环境。
cases.limits: 固件许可不覆盖所有云服务、声音、产品设计或商标。演示不能证明量产可靠性、儿童适用性或法规符合性。
evaluation: 测试噪声、打断、延迟与断网。
记录语音和模型服务费用。
规划固件恢复、密钥轮换与服务终止。
sources: 小智 ESP32 GitHub 仓库

cases.title: Unitree：选购机器人前核实开发权限
cases.label: 官方 SDK 参考
cases.summary: 公开 SDK 帮助科研买家更准确地询问版本、兼容性与支持。
cases.facts: Unitree 发布了 SDK2 及开发者文档中心，可作为评估软件接口和受支持流程的起点。
cases.lesson: 采购需求应注明机器人确切版本、权限、配件与软件环境，并包含培训、备件及本地操作人员。
cases.limits: 公开 SDK 不意味着所有版本都有相同开发权限。海外演示视频不能证明自主生产效率，也不是 CNPS 客户订单的证据。
evaluation: 取得型号与 SDK 权限的书面确认。
从仿真和有人监督的测试开始。
约定急停、工作空间与支持责任。
sources: 海外媒体 X 信号 · 2026年4月14日

resources.description: 详细战略方案：32个逻辑章节，附来源参考与透明修订记录。

solutions.title: 面向团队的 AI 会议设备
solutions.short: 批量采购前，比较录音设备、订阅归属与团队工作流程。
solutions.question: 哪款设备适合我们的团队？
overview: 这一页面向准备为团队采购 AI 录音设备（如 TicNote 系列）的管理者与经销商。个人试用一台录音笔很容易，但团队采购要回答另一组问题：订阅归谁、纪要谁来审、导出去哪里、成员离职后账号如何处理。我们建议先用一个小规模、可衡量的试点回答这些问题，再决定型号与数量。
CNPS 提供的是选型与试点方法、目的地供货核实与正式报价；转写表现、企业功能与批量条款以确切型号和书面报价为准。我们不会用厂商演示或他人的使用体验替代你们自己的测试结果。

scenarios.title: 跨语言的项目例会
scenarios.text: 团队在中文、英文或阿拉伯语之间切换开会，需要先确认设备在真实口音与专业术语下的转写表现，以及纠错所需时间是否可接受。

scenarios.title: 外勤与客户拜访记录
scenarios.text: 销售或工程人员在噪声环境中记录沟通内容。需要测试距离、噪声与电量表现，并明确录音告知与取得同意的流程。

scenarios.title: 经销商为客户配置批量订单
scenarios.text: 渠道伙伴需要在出货前确认目的地兼容性、订阅激活方式、保修处理与更换流程，并把这些写进供货条款。

solutions.deliverable: 更清晰的设备与订阅候选清单
solutions.input: 目的地国家、团队人数、会议语言、录音环境与目标日期。
checks: 比较确切型号及包含的订阅。
测试转写质量，以及修正纪要所需的时间。
确认导出格式、账号归属与转移方式。
确认地区供货、保修与批量采购条款。

steps.title: 确定试点小组与会议样本
steps.text: 选择 3–5 位能代表典型用户的成员，覆盖真实语言、会议室大小与远程通话场景。试点前先记录现有做纪要的耗时，作为对比基线。

steps.title: 在同一批会议上比较候选型号
steps.text: 用同样的会议样本测试候选设备与所含订阅，记录遗漏发言、姓名错误与行动项错误，以及修正到可用纪要所需的分钟数。

steps.title: 核对数据流程与账号归属
steps.text: 逐项检查导出格式、存储位置、分享与删除方式，确认订阅能否转移、是否有团队管理功能，以及成员离职后由谁控制录音。

steps.title: 形成候选清单并申请报价
steps.text: 把型号、数量、目的地、语言与时间要求整理成报价需求。CNPS 据此核实供货与批量条款，并按确切型号提供书面报价。

mistakes.title: 把转写速度当作节省时间
mistakes.text: 转写快不等于纪要可用。只有把修正、分发与行动项跟进的时间一起计入，才能判断团队是否真的省下了时间。

mistakes.title: 用消费级功能推断团队管理能力
mistakes.text: 账号转移、集中管理与企业功能因型号和订阅方案而异，应在下单前对所选型号逐项书面确认，而不是默认具备。

mistakes.title: 忽略录音告知与同意
mistakes.text: 不同国家和会议场景对录音有不同要求。试点开始前就应明确告知方式、同意记录与敏感内容的处理边界。

glossary.title: 确切型号
glossary.text: 报价单上写明的具体型号与版本，包括地区版本、颜色与随附方案。同名设备可能搭配不同的订阅与保修条款。

glossary.title: 随附订阅
glossary.text: 与设备捆绑的转写或纪要方案、有效期，以及到期后的处理方式。续费价格与付费方应记入试点记录。

glossary.title: 订阅归属
glossary.text: 方案绑定在个人账号还是组织名下，以及成员离职时能否转移。

glossary.title: 团队管理功能
glossary.text: 添加与移除用户、管理共享纪要、代他人导出等集中管理能力。是否具备取决于型号与方案。

glossary.title: 修正时间
glossary.text: 编辑者把原始转写整理成团队可以执行的纪要所需的分钟数。它比转写速度更能反映实际效果。

glossary.title: 导出格式
glossary.text: 纪要可以导出的文件类型与去向，如文本、DOCX、PDF 或云端文件夹，以及录音本身能否导出。

glossary.title: 录音告知与同意
glossary.text: 如何告知参会者会议正在录音，以及如何按当地规定与公司政策留存他们的同意记录。

glossary.title: 保修与换机（RMA）
glossary.text: 目的地国家由谁处理故障设备、换机需要多久，以及团队部署是否需要备用机。

metrics.title: 每场会议的基线分钟数
metrics.text: 试点前记录当前一份典型纪要从会议结束到分发所需的时间。之后所有比较都以这个数字为参照。

metrics.title: 每份转写的修正分钟数
metrics.text: 对每场录音会议，记录从打开原始转写到形成团队认可纪要所用的分钟数。比较各设备的中位数，而不是最好的一次。

metrics.title: 遗漏发言与姓名错误
metrics.text: 统计每场会议遗漏的决定、说话人归属错误、姓名与产品术语拼写错误，并注明哪些语言和会议室出错最多。

metrics.title: 行动项准确率
metrics.text: 核对生成的行动项是否与会上商定的一致，包括负责人和日期。负责人写错的纪要会制造工作，而不是节省工作。

metrics.title: 电量、距离与故障事件
metrics.text: 记录每场会议后的电量、距离与噪声条件，以及每一次录音、同步或导出失败，让硬件可靠性有据可查。

solutions.boundaries: 团队管理和企业功能因产品而异。下单前应按所选型号逐项确认。

faq.question: CNPS 能保证某款设备的转写准确率吗？
faq.answer: 不能。准确率取决于语言、口音、噪声与术语，厂商公布的数字不能替代你们自己的会议样本。我们建议按上述流程在真实会议上测试。

faq.question: 批量采购前一定要先试点吗？
faq.answer: 我们建议先用少量设备做有代表性的试点。它能在承诺数量之前暴露订阅归属、导出与噪声环境等问题，成本远低于批量退换。

faq.question: 报价需要提供哪些信息？
faq.answer: 目的地国家、预计数量、主要用途、会议语言、期望时间，以及是否需要先寄样品。信息越具体，供货核实与条款确认越快。

faq.question: 设备试点应持续多久？
faq.answer: 两到四周的正常会议通常足以覆盖口音、会议室类型与远程通话，并让团队进入真实的纪要流程。更短的试点往往反映的是新鲜感，而不是日常使用。

faq.question: 同一台设备能同时服务中文、英文和阿拉伯语会议吗？
faq.answer: 语言支持因型号与方案而异，实际表现又因口音和术语而不同。请在同一台设备上测试你们真正使用的每种语言，而不是只看支持语言列表。

faq.question: 试点之后订阅应归谁所有？
faq.answer: 下单前就要决定。如果纪要属于组织，方案就应集中管理并可转移。个人账号起步简单，但成员离职后更难收回。

solutions.title: 以企业文档为依据的知识助手
solutions.short: 围绕真实问题、访问权限与来源依据，定义私有知识或支持流程。
solutions.question: AI 能依据我们的文档回答吗？
overview: 这一页面向希望让 AI 依据企业自有文档回答问题的 IT 负责人、服务商与业务负责人。产品手册、内部制度、客服知识库都可能成为语料，但真正决定价值的不是模型名称，而是问题集是否真实、权限是否清晰、引用是否可核对。
CNPS 协助界定评估范围、准备评估题集与验收方式，并在需要时结合 FastGPT 等开源方案讨论实施。Dify、RAGFlow、Qwen 与 DeepSeek 等公开项目是研究起点，不是 CNPS 已交付的客户项目；实施范围与软件许可需另行约定。

scenarios.title: 产品手册与技术支持问答
scenarios.text: 售后或技术支持团队需要从多版本手册中快速找到准确答案，并能看到出处。评估重点是版本冲突的处理，以及引用是否真正支持答案。

scenarios.title: 内部制度与流程查询
scenarios.text: 员工询问报销、审批或合规流程。评估重点是权限边界：不同角色只能检索到自己应当看到的文档，过时制度需被及时下线。

scenarios.title: 多语言询盘初筛
scenarios.text: 出海团队收到中、英、阿等语言的询盘，需要依据产品资料给出初步回答再交给人工复核。评估重点是目标语言表现与拒答行为。

solutions.deliverable: 范围明确的知识助手评估
solutions.input: 已获授权的示例文档、目标语言、预计用户、部署要求与业务负责人。
checks: 建立包含参考答案的评估题集。
核验引用、模型版本与拒答行为。
测试文档权限和更新流程。
比较完整运行成本与人工审核时间。

steps.title: 确定单一任务与业务负责人
steps.text: 选一个流程、一批已授权文档和一位对答案质量负责的人。识别过时与相互矛盾的版本，先决定哪份文档是权威来源。

steps.title: 在调优前建立评估题集
steps.text: 参照资料中心的方法准备题集：日常事实题、跨文档比较题、证据不足应拒答的题，以及权限限制测试题。题集与阈值在看到结果前约定。

steps.title: 用同一题集比较候选方案
steps.text: 固定文档、提示与模型版本，由业务审核人比较正确性、引用支持、拒答与延迟，并记录人工修正每个答案所需的时间。

steps.title: 明确运营与成本后再扩大范围
steps.text: 记录由谁更新内容、批准访问、审核错误答案，并梳理每一次外部模型调用。把部署、推理、导入、支持与人工审核计入完整成本，再决定是否推广。

mistakes.title: 用公开榜单代替自己的数据测试
mistakes.text: 模型排名反映的是通用任务，不是你们的文档、术语与语言。同一题集下的表现，才是选型依据。

mistakes.title: 在看到结果后替换难题
mistakes.text: 把失败案例从题集里删掉会让评估失真。保留失败结果，把调优题与留出测试题分开，才能知道助手上线后的真实表现。

mistakes.title: 把开源可用等同于可以随意商用
mistakes.text: 开源项目的许可各有附加条件，例如多租户与品牌展示限制。上线前应核对确切版本的许可与托管服务条款。

glossary.title: 评估集
glossary.text: 在任何调优之前商定的固定问题清单，附带期望答案、来源与通过标准。它是衡量每个候选方案的统一尺子。

glossary.title: 依据检索的生成（RAG）
glossary.text: 助手先从你们的文档中检索段落，再据此回答，而不是只依赖通用训练数据的做法。

glossary.title: 引用
glossary.text: 助手为答案给出的来源。只有审阅者打开后确认被引段落确实支持该陈述，这条引用才算有效。

glossary.title: 拒答行为
glossary.text: 文档中没有答案时助手的表现。正确拒答算通过；编造答案即使听起来合理也算不通过。

glossary.title: 权限边界
glossary.text: 每个用户角色只能检索其被允许查看的文档，需要用针对角色的问题来测试。

glossary.title: 业务负责人
glossary.text: 对答案质量、文档更新以及扩大或停止决定负责的具名人员。

glossary.title: 留出测试
glossary.text: 在调优阶段不使用、只在最后运行的问题，用来观察助手面对未经调整的问题时的表现。

glossary.title: 完整运行成本
glossary.text: 每月的托管、推理、文档导入、许可、支持与人工审阅时间合计，而不只是模型 API 价格。

metrics.title: 评估集上的正确率
metrics.text: 按业务审阅者的判断回答正确的问题占比，并分别报告日常问题、跨文档比较与目标语言问题的结果。

metrics.title: 引用支持率
metrics.text: 打开后确实支持答案的引用占比。带有装饰性引用的答案按“无支持”计算。

metrics.title: 正确拒答次数
metrics.text: 面对文档中没有答案的问题，助手拒答的次数，以及编造答案的次数。

metrics.title: 权限测试结果
metrics.text: 针对角色的问题中，用户能检索到权限之外文档的次数。可接受的数字是零。

metrics.title: 每个答案的审阅分钟数与成本
metrics.text: 审阅者检查或修正一个答案的平均时间，加上每月的托管、推理与文档导入成本。

solutions.boundaries: 实施范围与软件许可需另行约定。开源可用并不代表拥有无限制转售权。

faq.question: 需要多少文档才能开始评估？
faq.answer: 从一个流程所需的已授权文档开始即可，通常几十份足以建立有意义的题集。范围小而权威，比大量未清理的资料更有价值。

faq.question: 评估会把我们的文档发给第三方吗？
faq.answer: 取决于部署方式与所选模型服务。即使应用自托管，模型或语音调用也可能向外部服务发送数据。我们建议先用非敏感文档评估，并逐项梳理数据流向。

faq.question: CNPS 会负责实施吗？
faq.answer: CNPS 先协助界定范围、题集与验收方式。实施能力、商业范围与软件许可根据具体需求另行约定，不会在评估阶段默认包含。

faq.question: 助手能完全运行在我们自己的服务器上吗？
faq.answer: 多种开源应用支持自托管部署，但它调用的语言模型、向量模型与语音模型仍可能是外部服务。先梳理每一次调用，再定义“本地部署”对你们的数据意味着什么。

faq.question: 文档更新后如何保持答案是最新的？
faq.answer: 指定内容更新负责人，明确废止文档如何从检索范围移除，并在每次重要更新后重跑部分评估集。没有更新机制的助手会悄悄过时。

faq.question: 可以评估哪些语言？
faq.answer: 中文、英文与阿拉伯语问题都可以纳入，但表现会因问题语言和文档语言而不同。把目标语言的问题写进评估集，而不是假设结果可以迁移。

solutions.title: 针对明确摄像任务的边缘 AI
solutions.short: 规划完整现场系统：摄像头、算力、网络、安装及可衡量的验收测试。
solutions.question: 边缘 AI 能在我们的现场运行吗？
overview: 这一页面向需要在工厂、养殖场、园区或商业场地部署摄像头识别任务的集成商与现场负责人。边缘 AI 的价值在于把识别放在现场完成，但它能否成立取决于整套系统：摄像头、算力、网络、安装、存储与运维，而不只是某块开发板的算力参数。
CNPS 协助整理现场需求、组织有代表性的现场测试并形成评估说明。Seeed 等厂商公开的部署参考展示了可能性，但不是 CNPS 已交付的项目，也不能保证在你们的光照、距离与网络条件下取得同样效果。

scenarios.title: 生产线或仓库的安全与合规监测
scenarios.text: 识别未佩戴防护装备、越界或异常停留等事件。评估重点是误报率能否让现场人员长期信任告警，以及夜间与逆光条件下的表现。

scenarios.title: 养殖与农业的持续观察
scenarios.text: 对动物或作物进行计数、行为或状态识别。评估重点是粉尘、湿度与光照变化对摄像头和算力设备的长期影响。

scenarios.title: 网络受限场地的本地识别
scenarios.text: 偏远站点或不允许视频上云的场地需要在本地完成识别、只上传结果。评估重点是断网时的行为、恢复方式与本地存储容量。

solutions.input: 摄像头类型、现场布局、光照、识别对象、网络条件与运营负责人。
checks: 约定检测任务和真实标注依据。
记录误报、漏报与端到端延迟。
测试光照变化、断网与恢复。
将安装、存储与支持计入成本。

steps.title: 约定检测任务与真实标注依据
steps.text: 用一句话写清要识别什么、在什么条件下、告警后由谁处理。约定如何产生真实标注，以及验收时可接受的误报与漏报水平。

steps.title: 完成现场勘查并采集代表性影像
steps.text: 参照边缘 AI 现场勘查表记录摄像头类型、安装位置、光照、距离、网络与供电。在不同时段采集影像，覆盖最不利的条件。

steps.title: 在真实影像上测试候选配置
steps.text: 用同一批影像比较候选摄像头与算力组合，记录误报、漏报与端到端延迟，并模拟光照变化、断网与设备重启。

steps.title: 核算完整成本并形成评估说明
steps.text: 把安装、布线、存储、备件、支持与运维人力计入每路摄像头和每个场地的成本。评估说明将成为报价与验收的共同依据。

mistakes.title: 用演示视频判断现场表现
mistakes.text: 演示视频通常在理想光照与距离下拍摄。你们的现场需要在最不利的条件下测试，才能知道系统能否长期运行。

mistakes.title: 只比较模型推理时间
mistakes.text: 端到端延迟包括采集、传输、推理与告警送达。只有测量完整链路，才能判断告警是否来得及让人处理。

mistakes.title: 漏算安装与运维成本
mistakes.text: 开发板价格只是一小部分。布线、防护外壳、存储、备件与远程维护往往决定项目能否持续。

glossary.title: 检测任务
glossary.text: 用一句话说明检测什么、在什么条件下、由谁处理结果。现场的其他一切都以它为衡量标准。

glossary.title: 真值
glossary.text: 经人工核实的、画面中实际发生情况的记录，用于判断每条告警是对还是错。

glossary.title: 误报与漏报
glossary.text: 误报是没有真实事件却触发告警；漏报是有真实事件却没有告警。两项都要统计，因为调整一项通常会影响另一项。

glossary.title: 端到端延迟
glossary.text: 从摄像头前发生事件到告警送达处理人员的时间，包括采集、传输、推理与推送。

glossary.title: 边缘设备 / 算力单元
glossary.text: 现场运行识别的计算机，如 Jetson 级别或 NPU 板卡。它在高温、灰尘与断电下的表现，比标称算力更重要。

glossary.title: 现场勘测
glossary.text: 在选择任何设备之前，对每个点位的摄像头类型、安装位置、光照、距离、网络与供电的结构化记录。

glossary.title: 验收标准
glossary.text: 事先商定的误报率、漏报率与延迟水平，决定安装是否被验收并付款。

glossary.title: 每路摄像头、每个现场的成本
glossary.text: 包含摄像头、算力、布线、防护箱、存储、备件、安装人工、支持与运维人员的完整数字。

metrics.title: 每路摄像头每天的误报数
metrics.text: 按摄像头和时段统计没有真实事件的告警。真正的阈值是员工能持续数周接受的水平，而不是厂商演示中的数字。

metrics.title: 对照真值的漏报率
metrics.text: 把告警与经核实的真实事件记录对比。分别报告白天、夜间、逆光以及你们采集到的最恶劣天气下的漏报。

metrics.title: 端到端延迟
metrics.text: 从画面中的事件发生到告警出现在处理人员的屏幕或手机上计时。记录中位数和最慢的 10%。

metrics.title: 在线率、断网与恢复
metrics.text: 记录每次设备重启、网络中断，以及识别和上传恢复所用的时间，包括本地存储是否保住了结果。

metrics.title: 每路摄像头与每个现场的成本
metrics.text: 把摄像头、算力、布线、防护箱、存储、备件、安装与支持加总，再除以你们实际计划运行的摄像头与现场数量。

solutions.boundaries: 硬件能力与演示视频不能保证在您的环境中达到同样效果，需要具有代表性的现场测试。

faq.question: 需要先购买设备才能评估吗？
faq.answer: 通常不需要。可以先完成现场勘查与影像采集，再用少量代表性设备做现场测试。在有明确任务与验收标准前大量采购，风险较高。

faq.question: CNPS 可以提供现成的识别方案吗？
faq.answer: CNPS 提供的是需求整理、现场评估方法与硬件采购渠道。识别任务是否可行取决于你们的现场条件，需要用代表性测试证明，而不是套用现成方案。

faq.question: 准确率能达到多少？
faq.answer: 我们不会在测试前给出准确率承诺。误报、漏报与延迟应在你们的真实影像上测得，并按事先约定的验收标准判断。

faq.question: 我们已有的摄像头能继续用吗？
faq.answer: 通常可以部分复用。分辨率、镜头角度、夜间表现与码流格式都会影响识别。把现有摄像头纳入现场测试，并做好更换在最恶劣条件下不达标设备的准备。

faq.question: 有代表性的现场测试需要多长时间？
faq.answer: 覆盖不同时段与天气的画面采集通常需要一到三周，比较本身还需要一到两周。压缩采集阶段是安装后结果无法复现的最常见原因。

faq.question: 视频和识别结果会如何处理？
faq.answer: 测试前先决定画面存储在哪里、保存多久、谁能查看、哪些数据会离开现场。本地识别可以减少数据传输，但保留与访问规则仍需要有人负责。

solutions.title: 语音交互：从想法到原型
solutions.short: 同时规划基于 ESP32 的语音设备及维持其运行所需的后端服务。
solutions.question: 如何制作语音设备原型？
overview: 这一页面向希望用 ESP32 等低成本硬件制作语音交互设备原型的产品团队、OEM 与展示项目负责人。开源固件让第一版原型变得触手可及，但设备只是服务的起点：语音识别、模型、内容与凭据管理等后端服务决定它能否持续工作。
CNPS 协助界定原型范围、梳理依赖项并规划测试。小智 ESP32 等开源项目是技术参考，不是 CNPS 的产品供应或服务合同；原型可用不等于量产承诺，产品测试、供货与商业权利须分别评估。

scenarios.title: 前台或展厅的问答终端
scenarios.text: 访客用语音询问展品、路线或开放时间。评估重点是噪声环境中的唤醒与识别、打断处理，以及内容更新由谁负责。

scenarios.title: 面向现有产品的语音配套原型
scenarios.text: 为现有产品增加语音入口，验证用户是否接受。评估重点是麦克风与外壳的声学配合、延迟，以及每次对话的服务成本。

scenarios.title: 多语言接待场景
scenarios.text: 接待中、英、阿等语言用户。评估重点是各语言的识别表现、语音合成质量与切换方式，以及内容是否已获授权。

solutions.deliverable: 原型范围与依赖项清单
solutions.input: 一项预期任务、用户、语言、声学条件、预计用量与维护负责人。
checks: 明确麦克风、扬声器、电源与网络。
梳理语音、模型和内容服务依赖。
测试打断、噪声与断网。
规划固件恢复、凭据管理和服务成本。

steps.title: 确定一项任务与授权内容
steps.text: 只做一件事：例如回答关于某一产品线的问题。准备已获授权的内容与预期问题，明确预计用户与用量。

steps.title: 明确硬件与依赖清单
steps.text: 参照语音原型规格书列出麦克风、扬声器、电源与网络需求，并梳理每一项语音、模型与内容服务的提供方、区域与计费方式。

steps.title: 在真实声学环境中测试
steps.text: 在实际使用地点测试噪声、距离、打断与断网情形，记录识别错误、响应延迟与恢复行为，而不是只在安静的办公室里演示。

steps.title: 规划生命周期后再谈下一步
steps.text: 约定固件恢复、凭据轮换、服务停用与内容更新方式，估算每台设备每月的服务成本。之后再讨论产品测试、供货与商业权利。

mistakes.title: 只算硬件成本
mistakes.text: ESP32 板卡便宜，但语音识别、模型与合成服务按用量计费。原型阶段就应记录每次对话的成本，避免推广后失控。

mistakes.title: 在安静环境中演示后直接推广
mistakes.text: 展厅、前台与街边的噪声与回声差别巨大。没有在目标环境中测试过的原型，不能作为部署依据。

mistakes.title: 忽略许可与商标边界
mistakes.text: 固件的开源许可不涵盖所使用的云服务、语音、产品设计或商标。面向公众发布前应逐项核对。

glossary.title: 唤醒词
glossary.text: 让设备从监听自己名字切换到处理请求的短语。噪声中的误唤醒与远距离的漏唤醒都需要测量。

glossary.title: 语音识别（ASR）
glossary.text: 把语音转成文字的服务。通常是按分钟或按请求计费的云服务，有各自的语言覆盖与服务区域。

glossary.title: 语音合成（TTS）
glossary.text: 生成语音回复的服务。音色质量、语言支持与面向公众使用的授权是三个独立问题。

glossary.title: 打断处理
glossary.text: 用户在设备仍在回复时说话会发生什么。处理不好会让演示在真实使用中显得迟缓。

glossary.title: 依赖清单
glossary.text: 设备调用的每一项外部服务的列表，包括提供方、区域、凭证负责人与计费方式，避免某项变更时无人知情。

glossary.title: 每次对话成本
glossary.text: 一次典型交互的识别、模型与合成费用之和，再乘以每台设备每月的预期对话量。

glossary.title: 固件恢复
glossary.text: 固件、凭证或服务地址变更时，如何在现场更新或恢复设备，而不必寄回。

glossary.title: 授权内容
glossary.text: 设备被允许回答的问题范围以及可以据以回答的材料，在原型面向公众之前与内容负责人商定。

metrics.title: 按环境统计的唤醒与识别错误
metrics.text: 在真实场所分别统计安静时段、噪声高峰以及每种语言下的误唤醒、漏唤醒与请求识别错误。

metrics.title: 响应延迟
metrics.text: 从用户说完一句话到语音回复开始的时间。记录中位数与最慢的情况，并注明延迟来自哪项服务。

metrics.title: 打断与恢复表现
metrics.text: 记录用户打断、回复中途断网以及设备重启时发生了什么，以及恢复可用需要多长时间。

metrics.title: 每次对话与每台设备每月的成本
metrics.text: 在原型阶段汇总典型交互的识别、模型与合成费用，并按预期对话量推算。

metrics.title: 内容覆盖率与拒答
metrics.text: 统计真实访客问题中落在授权内容范围内的数量、被正确拒答的数量，以及超出范围却被回答的数量。

solutions.boundaries: 原型可用不等于承诺量产。产品测试、供货与商业权利须分别评估。

faq.question: CNPS 会为我们生产语音设备吗？
faq.answer: CNPS 在原型阶段协助界定范围、依赖与测试。量产涉及产品测试、供货、认证与商业权利，需要在原型验证后另行评估与约定。

faq.question: 原型适合面向儿童或公众吗？
faq.answer: 演示可用不能证明内容安全、儿童适用性或法规符合性。面向公众部署前，应针对内容边界、隐私与安全做专门评估。

faq.question: 断网后设备还能工作吗？
faq.answer: 取决于架构。多数语音功能依赖后端服务，断网时应有明确的提示与恢复行为。这是测试中必须覆盖的情形。

faq.question: 第一个原型需要什么硬件？
faq.answer: 一块 ESP32 级别的开发板、麦克风阵列、扬声器和稳定供电通常足以测试交互本身。外壳声学与工业级元器件要等任务与环境确认之后再考虑。

faq.question: 设备能接入我们自己的模型或知识库吗？
faq.answer: 通常可以，因为固件调用的是你们配置的后端服务。需要评估的是这个后端能否在可接受的延迟与成本内正确回答，其测试方法与知识助手相同。

faq.question: 现场测试前应准备什么？
faq.answer: 授权内容、预期问题清单、目标场所最繁忙的时段、记录每次交互的方法，以及负责判断哪些回答可接受的人。

solutions.title: 面向科研与受控试点的机器人
solutions.short: 采购前明确硬件版本、SDK 权限、配件与本地支持。
solutions.question: 我们的机器人实验室需要什么？
overview: 这一页面向计划为高校实验室、研究机构或企业创新团队采购四足机器人、机械臂等平台的负责人。公开的 SDK 与演示视频让机器人研究看起来门槛更低，但采购时真正需要写清的是：确切版本、开发权限、配件、培训与本地支持由谁负责。
CNPS 协助整理配置与支持清单，并核实供货与目的地条款。宇树 SDK2、UFACTORY xArm SDK 等公开资料是评估起点，不代表每个产品版本都有相同权限，也不是 CNPS 已交付的客户订单。现场安全与集成需要合格负责人。

scenarios.title: 运动控制与感知算法研究
scenarios.text: 实验室需要在真实平台上验证算法。评估重点是所选版本是否开放底层控制接口，以及操作系统与 SDK 版本的兼容性。

scenarios.title: 受控的抓取与装配试点
scenarios.text: 用机械臂完成有限工件的取放或装配。评估重点是工件、夹爪、负载、可达范围与相机布置，以及可重复的成功率记录。

scenarios.title: 教学与人才培养
scenarios.text: 多名学生轮流使用同一平台。评估重点是培训、备件、应急流程与有人监督的使用规范，而不只是机器人本体。

solutions.input: 研究任务、确切平台、负载、工作空间、开发权限、目的地与受训操作人员。
checks: 书面确认型号与开发权限。
检查操作系统与 SDK 兼容性。
计入工具、工装、备件与培训。
定义有人监督的测试及应急流程。

steps.title: 写清研究任务与确切平台
steps.text: 用任务描述反推需求：负载、工作空间、传感器、开发权限与目的地。名称相同的机器人不同版本权限可能不同，务必写明确切型号。

steps.title: 书面确认 SDK 权限与兼容性
steps.text: 向供应方索取所选版本的开发权限、支持的操作系统与 SDK 版本的书面确认，并核对实验室现有的软件环境。

steps.title: 从仿真与有人监督的测试开始
steps.text: 先在仿真中验证流程，再在限定工作空间内做有人监督的测试。记录成功尝试与全部失败情形，约定急停与应急流程。

steps.title: 把完整配置写进采购需求
steps.text: 参照机器人采购资料把工具、工装、备件、培训、运输与本地支持列入清单，明确安全与维护的负责人，再申请报价。

mistakes.title: 以为公开 SDK 适用于所有版本
mistakes.text: 教育版、标准版与开发版的接口开放程度可能不同。采购前应按确切版本取得书面确认。

mistakes.title: 只采购机器人本体
mistakes.text: 夹爪、工装、相机、备件、培训与运输往往决定项目能否开展。缺少任何一项都可能让设备闲置数月。

mistakes.title: 用演示视频推断自主能力
mistakes.text: 国际演示视频展示的是可能性，不是自主生产力的证明。研究任务能否完成，取决于你们的算法、场景与操作能力。

glossary.title: 确切版本
glossary.text: 报价单上写明的具体产品版本，如教育版、标准版或开发者版。机身相同的不同版本可能开放不同的接口。

glossary.title: 开发者权限 / 底层控制
glossary.text: 该版本是否允许你的代码直接控制关节、电机或步态，而不只是通过上层应用或示教器操作。

glossary.title: SDK 版本兼容性
glossary.text: 平台支持的操作系统、ROS 发行版、Python 与库版本，需要与实验室现有环境逐项核对。

glossary.title: 负载与臂展
glossary.text: 机械臂或机器人能承载的质量与可覆盖的工作空间，应按包含夹爪与相机的确切配置给出。

glossary.title: 末端执行器 / 夹爪
glossary.text: 安装在机械臂末端用于完成任务的工具。通常单独订购，直接决定你们研究中的工件能否被抓取。

glossary.title: 受限工作区
glossary.text: 测试期间机器人可以运行的物理区域，配有防护、急停装置以及关于谁可以进入的明确规则。

glossary.title: 可重复成功率
glossary.text: 在相同条件下多次运行中完成任务的尝试占比，需记录每一次失败，而不是只保留最好的一次演示。

glossary.title: 本地支持与备件
glossary.text: 在你们所在国家由谁维修平台、零件到货需要多久，以及首次测试前应备哪些耗材。

metrics.title: 已收到的书面确认
metrics.text: 跟踪供应商已对确切版本书面确认的项目：开发者权限、支持的操作系统、SDK 版本、保修与目的地条款。

metrics.title: 兼容性结果
metrics.text: 记录 SDK 能否在实验室现有机器上安装运行、需要哪些版本，以及发出第一条指令之前的配置耗时。

metrics.title: 任务成功率与失败日志
metrics.text: 在相同条件下统计成功与失败的尝试次数及每次失败的原因，让自主能力的判断建立在重复运行上，而不是一次演示。

metrics.title: 安全事件与险情
metrics.text: 记录受监督测试中的每次急停、越界与非计划动作，以及之后流程做了哪些调整。

metrics.title: 到首次实验的时间与成本
metrics.text: 测量从下单到完成第一次实验的日历时间与完整成本，包括配件、培训、运输、清关以及等待零件的闲置周数。

solutions.boundaries: 公开 SDK 不代表每个产品版本都有相同权限。现场安全和集成需要合格负责人。

faq.question: CNPS 能提供哪些机器人平台？
faq.answer: CNPS 按需求核实可供货的确切版本、配件与目的地条款，并整理配置清单。任何平台的供货与权限以供应方书面确认为准。

faq.question: 需要提前准备哪些现场条件？
faq.answer: 限定的工作空间、急停与防护措施、合格的操作人员以及维护负责人。这些应在设备到达前落实，而不是到货后再补。

faq.question: 可以先租用或试用吗？
faq.answer: 是否有试用或租用选项取决于平台与地区。我们建议在询盘中说明研究任务与时间安排，以便一并核实可行的评估方式。

faq.question: 应该从机械臂还是四足机器人开始？
faq.answer: 取决于研究任务。抓取、装配与工件研究指向机械臂；运动控制、感知与户外导航指向足式平台。先把任务写下来，再让平台跟随任务。

faq.question: 一份典型的机器人报价包含什么？
faq.answer: 确切版本、开发者权限、夹爪与相机等配件、备件、培训、运输与目的地条款，每项单独列行。报价单上没有的项目，应视为不包含。

faq.question: 交付后的维护如何规划？
faq.answer: 指定维护负责人，按供应商建议备好耗材，确认在你们所在国家由谁维修以及零件到货时间，并从第一周起记录每一次故障。

solutionsIndex.chooseText: 每个方案都从一个采购问题出发。下表列出你会得到什么、需要准备什么以及第一件要核实的事，帮助你找到最接近自身情况的页面。
solutionsIndex.prepText: 无论选择哪个方案，这五件事都能让第一次沟通更有效。

prep.title: 明确一个任务
prep.text: 描述你想改善的单一流程或现场，而不是整个组织。范围越窄，试点越可衡量，报价越准确。

prep.title: 确定目的地与时间
prep.text: 国家、预计数量以及需要看到结果的日期，决定了供货、运输方式，以及先寄样品是否现实。

prep.title: 记录当前基线
prep.text: 这项工作现在需要多长时间、多久失败一次、成本是多少。没有基线，任何试点都无法证明改善。

prep.title: 确定决策负责人
prep.text: 负责评判试点并签署订单的人。他们的验收标准应在测试开始前写下来。

prep.title: 区分硬性要求与偏好
prep.text: 数据存放地、语言支持、保修与管理功能中不可妥协的部分应写进询盘；其余都可以讨论。

solutionsIndex.termsText: 同样的词出现在每个方案页、资料中心与我们的报价中。这里说明我们的具体含义。

terms.title: 试点
terms.text: 在承诺任何数量之前，用真实用户、真实数据与商定指标进行的小规模、限时测试。

terms.title: 基线
terms.text: 试点之前对工作现状的测量结果，是之后所有比较的参照。

terms.title: 验收标准
terms.text: 事先商定的可衡量结果，决定试点或交付是否被接受。

terms.title: 确切型号或版本
terms.text: 报价单上写明的具体产品版本。同名产品在功能、权限与保修上可能不同。

terms.title: 目的地供货
terms.text: 产品能否在买方所在国家供货、激活、保修与支持，报价前需要核实。

terms.title: 询价需求（RFQ）
terms.text: 关于任务、数量、目的地、语言与时间的书面摘要，CNPS 据此准备正式报价。

terms.title: 行业参考
terms.text: 用于展示可能性的公开案例或开源项目。它不是 CNPS 已交付的客户项目，也不承诺相同结果。

terms.title: 完整成本
terms.text: 在计划运行方案的整个期间内，硬件、订阅、托管、安装、培训、支持与审阅时间的总和。

cases.title: Dify في اليابان: من التجارب إلى سير العمل المؤسسي
cases.label: قصة عميل نشرها المورّد
cases.summary: تربط قصة عميل منشورة بين بناء سير العمل والتبني والحوكمة على مستوى الشركة.
cases.facts: تصف قصة Kakaku.com المنشورة لدى Dify اعتماد Dify Enterprise لتنظيم تطوير تطبيقات الذكاء الاصطناعي. ويوفر مستودع GitHub وثائق لسير العمل والاسترجاع والاستضافة الذاتية. القصة رواية من المورّد وليست تدقيقاً مستقلاً.
cases.lesson: السؤال المفيد للمشتري هو كيف يصبح سير العمل قابلاً للاستخدام الجماعي: من يملكه، ومن يصل إلى البيانات، وكيف تُصعّد الأخطاء؟ تقترح CNPS البدء بسير عمل واحد للمستندات أو الدعم ومجموعة تقييم متفق عليها.
cases.limits: هذا ليس مشروعاً نفذته CNPS. لا تثبت بيانات التبني المعلنة نتيجة مشروع عميل جديد. يتضمن ترخيص Dify شروطاً إضافية للاستخدام متعدد المستأجرين والعلامة التجارية للواجهة.
evaluation: استخدم مستندات مصرحاً بها ومجموعة أسئلة ثابتة.
قس دقة الاستشهادات ووقت التصحيح البشري.
اختبر الصلاحيات والامتناع عن الإجابة عند غياب الأدلة.

cases.title: Qwen وDeepSeek: تسهيل التقييم الأول
cases.label: مرجع للمصدر المفتوح وقنوات الانتشار
cases.summary: تخفض المواد التقنية بالإنجليزية وقنوات التقييم العامة الجهد اللازم لتجربة نموذج.
cases.facts: يحتفظ Qwen3 وDeepSeek-R1 بمستودعات عامة تضم معلومات النماذج والاستخدام. ويربط منشور Qwen الرسمي على X إعلان نموذج بالاستخدام المحلي والتجربة عبر الإنترنت. ويسجل منشور عام مرتبط بـArena دخول DeepSeek-R1 إلى قناة تقييم دولية.
cases.lesson: يحتاج المشتري إلى مهمة قابلة لإعادة الإنتاج وإصدار محدد للنموذج وحدود للتكلفة. قيّم النماذج المرشحة بالمستندات والأسئلة نفسها، بما فيها أسئلة ينبغي الامتناع عن إجابتها.
cases.limits: لا تثبت هذه المراجع الإيرادات أو التفوق الحالي للنموذج أو الأداء على بياناتك. تحقق من نقطة التحقق المحددة للنموذج وترخيصه والبنية التحتية وشروط الخدمة.
evaluation: ثبت مجموعة البيانات والتعليمات وإصدارات النماذج.
قارن الصحة والاستشهادات وزمن الاستجابة والتكلفة لكل مهمة مكتملة.
اختبر اللغة المستهدفة والاستخدام المتزامن الواقعي.

cases.title: RAGFlow: قيّم طبقة المستندات أولاً
cases.label: مرجع تقني مفتوح المصدر
cases.summary: مرجع عملي لسير عمل الاسترجاع الذي يحتاج إلى إجابات قابلة للتتبع من مستندات معقدة.
cases.facts: يصف مستودع RAGFlow معالجة المستندات والاسترجاع والاستشهاد بالمصادر، مع تعليمات للاستضافة الذاتية. إنه مصدر تقني لتقييم سير عمل المستندات، وليس دليلاً على نشر لدى عميل لـCNPS.
cases.lesson: تحتوي أدلة المنتجات على اختلافات بين الإصدارات ووحدات واستثناءات. قبل اختيار نموذج، حدد المستند المعتمد وكيفية إزالة المعلومات القديمة.
cases.limits: لا يضمن دعم المستندات المعلن في مستودع جودة الاستخراج من مسح ضوئي أو جدول بعينه. ينبغي التحقق من احتياجات الحوسبة وإصدارات الاعتماديات للإصدار المختار.
evaluation: أدرج الجداول والمستندات الممسوحة والإصدارات المتعارضة.
تحقق من أن المقطع المستشهد به يدعم الإجابة المحددة.
اختبر التحديثات والحذف وحدود الوصول.

cases.title: Seeed وIntflow: حل محلي مبني على أجهزة الحوسبة الطرفية
cases.label: مرجع نشر أصدره المورّد
cases.summary: يوضح مرجع مراقبة الماشية التعاون بين الخبرة التطبيقية والأجهزة الطرفية.
cases.facts: تصف مجموعة دراسات حالات Seeed المستضافة لدى PNY حل Intflow لمراقبة الماشية، وتذكر عمليات نشر في كوريا الجنوبية وإسبانيا واليابان والنمسا وبولندا. وتحدد جهاز Seeed reComputer ضمن الحل.
cases.lesson: النمط القابل للاستفادة هو تولّي متخصص محلي التطبيق والعلاقة مع الموقع، مع دعم مورّد الأجهزة لمنصة الجهاز. حدد نطاق النظام كاملاً، بما يشمل الكاميرات والخدمة المستمرة.
cases.limits: المادة منشورة من المورّد، ولا نستخدم التحسينات المعلنة فيها كتوقعات. وهي لا تثبت علاقة توزيع مع CNPS أو ملاءمة موقع جديد.
evaluation: حدد الحيوانات أو الأجسام وظروف المراقبة.
استخدم لقطات تمثل الواقع مع بيانات مرجعية متفق عليها.
احسب التكلفة الإجمالية لكل كاميرا ولكل موقع.
sources: مجموعة حالات Seeed المستضافة لدى PNY

cases.title: Seeed: ربط عرض الأجهزة بالوثائق الهندسية
cases.label: مرجع هندسي رسمي ومنشور على X
cases.summary: يصبح العرض مفيداً للشراء عندما تتضح إعداداته ومسار تنفيذه الهندسي.
cases.facts: يصف منشور Seeed الرسمي على X إعداداً طرفياً بأربع كاميرات. ويوفر مستودع Wiki العام وخدمة التخصيص مراجع مستقلة للهندسة ودورة الحياة، من المتطلبات إلى التحقق والإنتاج.
cases.lesson: يمكن لمقطع قصير تقديم احتمال تقني. ثم ينبغي أن توفر صفحة الشراء مخطط النظام وقائمة الأجهزة وافتراضات البيئة وخطة اختبار يمكن للمهندس تقييمها.
cases.limits: منشور X ادعاء عرض توضيحي. لا يثبت قياسات أداء مستقلة أو حلاً جاهزاً من CNPS. يجب التحقق من التوافق على التكوين المختار.
evaluation: حدد واجهات الكاميرات ووحدة الحوسبة وإصدارات البرمجيات.
قس زمن الاستجابة الكلي، وليس استدلال النموذج وحده.
اختبر التعافي من الأعطال والتشغيل المستمر.

cases.title: XiaoZhi ESP32: الجهاز بداية الخدمة
cases.label: مرجع تقني مفتوح المصدر
cases.summary: تسهّل البرامج الثابتة المفتوحة بناء نموذج صوتي أولي، بينما تحدد خيارات الخلفية ودورة الحياة فائدته.
cases.facts: يوفر مستودع XiaoZhi ESP32 برامج ثابتة للواجهات الصوتية ووثائق متعددة اللغات. ويصف ملف README اتصالات النماذج وMCP. المستودع مرجع للبرنامج الثابت، وليس عقد توريد منتج كامل أو خدمة.
cases.lesson: لنموذج استقبال أو معرض، ابدأ بمهمة واحدة ومحتوى مصرح به. حدد الميكروفون والشبكة والخلفية إلى جانب الغلاف، ثم اختبر البيئة الصوتية الفعلية.
cases.limits: لا يشمل ترخيص البرنامج الثابت جميع الخدمات السحابية أو الأصوات أو تصاميم المنتجات أو العلامات التجارية. ولا يثبت العرض موثوقية الإنتاج أو الملاءمة للأطفال أو الامتثال التنظيمي.
evaluation: اختبر الضوضاء والمقاطعة وزمن الاستجابة وانقطاع الشبكة.
وثّق رسوم خدمات الصوت والنموذج.
خطط لاستعادة البرنامج الثابت وتدوير المفاتيح وإيقاف الخدمة.

cases.title: Unitree: تحقق من صلاحيات التطوير قبل اختيار روبوت
cases.label: مرجع SDK رسمي
cases.summary: تساعد حزم SDK العامة المشترين البحثيين على إعداد أسئلة أدق عن الإصدارات والتوافق والدعم.
cases.facts: تنشر Unitree حزمة SDK2 ومركز وثائق للمطورين. ويوفران نقطة انطلاق لتقييم واجهات البرمجيات ومسارات العمل المدعومة.
cases.lesson: ينبغي أن تحدد متطلبات الشراء إصدار الروبوت الدقيق والصلاحيات والملحقات وبيئة البرمجيات. أدرج التدريب وقطع الغيار والمشغّل المحلي، إلى جانب جسم الروبوت.
cases.limits: لا تعني حزمة SDK العامة أن جميع الإصدارات تتيح صلاحيات تطوير متطابقة. ولا تثبت عروض الفيديو الدولية إنتاجية مستقلة أو طلب عميل لدى CNPS.
evaluation: احصل على تأكيد مكتوب لرمز المنتج وصلاحيات SDK.
ابدأ بالمحاكاة والاختبارات الخاضعة للإشراف.
اتفق على إيقاف الطوارئ ومساحة العمل ومسؤولية الدعم.

cases.title: UFACTORY xArm: حدد خلية العمل كاملة
cases.label: مرجع SDK رسمي
cases.summary: حزمة SDK الموجهة للمطورين أحد مدخلات قرار التكامل، الذي يحتاج أيضاً إلى الأدوات وظروف الموقع.
cases.facts: يوفر مستودع xArm Python SDK واجهات ووثائق وأمثلة لروبوتات UFACTORY، وهو مرجع تقني مباشر لتكامل البرمجيات.
cases.lesson: لتجربة التقاط ووضع خاضعة للتحكم، حدد قطعة العمل والقابض والحمولة والمدى وزمن الدورة وترتيب الكاميرات. قس الأداء القابل للتكرار بأجسام تمثل الاستخدام الفعلي.
cases.limits: حزمة SDK ليست تصميماً كاملاً للسلامة ولا خلية عمل جاهزة للإنتاج. لا يثبت هذا المرجع شراكة مع CNPS أو نتيجة مضمونة للمهمة.
evaluation: سجل المحاولات الناجحة وجميع الإخفاقات.
أدرج تكاليف الأدوات والتجهيزات والكاميرا والتكامل.
عيّن مسؤولاً مؤهلاً لسلامة الموقع والصيانة.

cases.title: من مسجل فردي إلى خطة شراء لفريق
cases.label: دليل CNPS لتقييم المنتجات
cases.summary: استخدم كتالوج CNPS الحالي نقطة انطلاق، ثم تحقق مما يحتاجه الفريق فعلياً.
cases.facts: يعرض موقع منتجات CNPS أجهزة تسجيل TicNote وأجهزة قابلة للارتداء، ويوفر جهة اتصال للبيع بالجملة. ينبغي التحقق من تفاصيل المنتج والاشتراك الحالية في صفحة المنتج المحدد وعرض السعر.
cases.lesson: ينبغي أن تختبر تجربة الفريق لغات الاجتماعات الفعلية والضوضاء ووقت تصحيح الملاحظات ومتطلبات التصدير وملكية الحساب. أدرج الاشتراك وعملية الدعم في المقارنة.
cases.limits: هذا دليل شراء وليس حالة عميل مكتملة. لا يُفترض وجود خصائص مؤسسية أو خصومات كمية أو تفويض أو توافر إقليمي دون تأكيد.
evaluation: اختر مجموعة صغيرة تمثل المستخدمين.
قس الاستخدام الفعلي وصافي الوقت الموفر بعد التصحيحات.
أكد إعادة تعيين الاشتراك ومعالجة الضمان.
